content.text:
Findings:

1. High: the new `commits.jsonl` entry is written too late to ever be included in the checkpoint that was just condensed. In `postCommitProcessSession`, `TransitionAndLog(...)` performs the condensation first, and only afterward do we append the sidecar entry (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:1325`). The condense path builds `WriteCommittedOptions` without `MetadataDir` at all (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:229`), and checkpoint persistence only copies sidecar files when `opts.MetadataDir != ""` (`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go:318`). So the current checkpoint never contains its own commit-log row; at best a later checkpoint could copy a stale local file, and the last commit in a session is lost entirely. That breaks the “timeline reconstruction” comment in practice.

Open question:

- I couldn’t find any reader/use-site for `readCommitLog`, so this branch currently looks write-only. If there’s a follow-up branch that consumes `commits.jsonl`, it should probably add an end-to-end post-commit test that verifies the just-created checkpoint contains the new entry.  

Verification: `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy -run 'TestAppendCommitLogEntry_CreatesAndAppends|TestReadCommitLog_NonexistentFile|TestCommitSubject'` passed.

content.text: I found one likely compatibility regression in the dual-write path. I’m pulling exact references from the v2 writer before I close this out.

Findings:

1. Medium: `CommitLog` is wired into shared `WriteCommittedOptions`, but the v2 writer still drops it. `CondenseSession` now passes `CommitLog` into both v1 and v2 writes (`[manual_commit_condensation.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:244)`), and the field is defined on the shared options struct (`[checkpoint.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/checkpoint.go:312)`). But `V2GitStore.writeMainSessionToSubdirectory` only writes `prompt.txt`, compact transcript, and `metadata.json`; it never persists `commits.jsonl` (`[v2_committed.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/v2_committed.go:334)`). If `checkpoints_v2` is enabled, the new timeline data exists in v1 only, so v2-backed reads/migration will silently lose it.

Open questions / residual risk:

- I don’t see any reader/API for `commits.jsonl` yet, so this is still largely write-side plumbing plus tests.
- I reran the targeted tests, including the new post-commit coverage and the checkpoint package tests; they passed.
